interest: From Roosevelt's 1941 birthday greeting to Hirohito to 1944 debate on the Emperor's postwar role.
overview: This file comprises State Department records classified under decimal file 894.001 (Political Affairs, Japan: Chief Executive / Sovereign), containing diplomatic communications, cross-reference sheets, and correspondence dating from May 1941 to July 1944. The materials include a May 1941 instruction to Tokyo transmitting President Franklin D. Roosevelt's birthday congratulations to Emperor Hirohito; a January 1944 cross-reference note regarding Anglo-American diplomatic discussions in London on former Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's speech proposing the Emperor's retention as a stabilizing postwar element; a February 1944 letter from the Division of Japanese Affairs refuting an alleged 1914 World War I prophecy by Premier Shigenobu Okuma; and a July 1944 telegram from Ambassador W. Averell Harriman in Moscow reporting Soviet press coverage of the newly formed Koiso-Yonai Cabinet and its presentation to the Emperor.

subfiles.about: The Secretary of State transmits to Ambassador Grew the text of President Roosevelt's birthday greeting to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 2168 quotes Roosevelt's April 29, 1941 birthday telegram of congratulations to Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 2168 to the American Ambassador in Tokyo quoting President Roosevelt's birthday telegram to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: A cross-reference file note refers to a London embassy report on British Foreign Office reactions to Joseph C. Grew's speech regarding the postwar role of the Japanese Emperor.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to London despatch No. 13430 (1944) on Clarke and Allison discussing Grew's speech on the Emperor's postwar role.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on conversation regarding Joseph C. Grew's speech on the Japanese Emperor as a postwar stabilizing force

subfiles.about: The Division of Japanese Affairs responds to an inquiry regarding an alleged 1914 prediction of a thirty-year war by Japanese Premier Shigenobu Okuma.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover (Chief, Division of Japanese Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Dickover tells Brown Landone that Okuma was Premier in August 1914, but no record shows he predicted a thirty-year war.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Brown Landone concerning Premier Shigenobu Okuma and alleged 1914 statement

subfiles.about: Ambassador Harriman transmits translations of Soviet press reports covering the formation and members of the Koiso-Yonai Cabinet presented to the Emperor.
subfiles.from: W. Averell Harriman (Ambassador to the USSR, Moscow)
subfiles.summary: Harriman relays Soviet press accounts of Domei reports on the Koiso-Yonai Cabinet's presentation to the Emperor on July 22, 1944 and Koiso's first radio address.
